instructions: User directive 2026-10-25: five encoder pilots on top of chamfer_lean_randmask (chlrm) on hammer, pick-place and bin-picking; descriptive, no adoption rule; adoption or expansion is the user's decision (directive 1). New rows use free capacity only at a priority strictly below every registered row; every new flag defaults to off with a bit-for-bit identity test; the frozen method and the chlrm definition are unchanged; the RL protocol is unchanged.
base: base.yaml + tasks/<task>.yaml + variants/chamfer_lean.yaml + variants/chamfer_lean_randmask.yaml (chlrm, runs/setup/mpf-definition-20261023.json), plus one variant file per arm

protocol.pretraining: 200k steps, seed 0 (train.steps=200000, train.seed=0), the chlrm row's settings
protocol.rl: DrM, 1M agent steps, seeds 2000-2002, proprioception as in the final comparison, the same evaluation schedule (every 10k), camera groups and episodes; rows copied from the chlrm reference rows

hn.definition: hard negatives: for each training sample (episode, first frame t0, stride s) one extra window of the same episode with the same stride and 2s+2 <= |t0'-t0| <= 40 simulator steps (no shared frame), drawn uniformly among the candidates that pass the robot-state rule; encoded from all 6 training cameras in training mode with the anchors' masking (uniform random 75 %, 48 of 192 temporal tokens, fresh masks per row as the anchors) and gradients; only in the InfoNCE denominator as extra columns (all-gathered like the features, invalid ones masked out, weight 1.0); positives stay 'same window, other cameras'; never decoded, rendered, given synthetic views, used in slot consistency or as a positive.

robot_state_rule.fields: robot state only: Meta-World obs[0:4] (hand xyz, gripper opening in [0,1]) = the RL proprio indices 0-3; DROID: probe_state[0:3] end-effector position and probe_state[6] normalised gripper position (s4d/data/hardneg.py ROBOT_COLUMNS)
robot_state_rule.valid_if: |hand(t0+2s) - hand(t0'+2s)| >= hardneg_min_hand_m (0.01 m) or |grip(t0+2s) - grip(t0'+2s)| >= hardneg_min_gripper (0.1)
robot_state_rule.no_valid_candidate: the negative is invalid and masked out

hn.pre_training_report: runs/setup/encp-hardneg-report-20261025.json (training episodes; kept candidate pairs 88.0 / 86.3 / 90.3 %, samples with a valid negative 97.8 / 95.9 / 98.3 %, hand displacement median 6.8 / 6.9 / 8.1 cm for hammer / pick-place / bin-picking); thresholds never tuned on any result

logging.hardneg_cosine: each anchor state vs its own sample's negative window from the same camera (valid samples)
logging.hardneg_valid_fraction: fraction of samples with a valid negative
logging.hardneg_within_episode_top1: pairwise cross-view form (the convention of the existing cross-view retrieval): for every ordered training-camera pair (a, b), a != b, the anchor from camera a is more similar (cosine) to its own window from camera b than to the negative window from camera b (two candidates, chance 0.5), over valid samples
logging.hardneg_hand_disp_mean: mean hand displacement of the valid negatives (m)
logging.hardneg_gallery_top1: gallery form (added after the Codex review, before any result): per anchor from camera a, its best match among its own window's other cameras beats its best match among all cameras of the negative window, the same camera a included

cs.definition: patch-local conv stem replacing the 16x16 stride-16 patchify convolution: per 16x16 patch independently, four 3x3 stride-2 convolutions 3 -> 32 -> 64 -> 128 -> 128 (padding 1, no bias), each followed by GroupNorm and GELU, then a 1x1 convolution (with bias) to the encoder width; same 64 tokens per frame, positional and temporal embeddings and ViT; receptive field inside the patch, so masking semantics are unchanged (Xiao et al., NeurIPS 2021 idea; their stem overlaps patches).

h2.definition: width 128, depth 8, 2 heads (head dim 64; chlrm 8 heads of 16); parameters and FLOPs unchanged

w4.definition: SinCro-shaped ViT body: width 256, depth 4, 4 heads (head dim 64), MLP 1024

common_h2_w4_w8: slot_dim stays 256 (slot_proj = Linear(width, 256)); patch 16; the decoder (width 128) and all losses; the same learning rate and schedule as chlrm

sizes.counter: torch.utils.flop_counter.FlopCounterMode on CPU, multiply-add = 2 FLOPs, three-frame observation / 3, eval mode, no masking: the counter of docs/BASELINES.md (chlrm reproduces its 1,726,592 parameters and 0.214980 GFLOPs/frame)

implementation_choices: hn masking: 'exactly the anchors' masking (uniform random 75 %, 48 of 192 temporal tokens)' is implemented as the same masking procedure: every negative row draws its own uniform random 48-of-192 mask through the same encoder call path as the anchors (as every anchor row draws its own); the anchors' visible-token indices are not copied to the negatives. Reading recorded before any result and reported to the user.
cs GroupNorm: 8 groups in every stem layer (unspecified in the directive; fixed before any result).
cs convolutions have no bias (each is followed by GroupNorm); the 1x1 projection has a bias.
cs stem parameters keep the module name patch_embed, so the optimizer's existing rule (no weight decay for names containing 'embed') applies to the stem as it applies to the patchify convolution.
cs computes the stem on every patch (also masked ones) and then keeps the visible tokens, exactly as patchify; masked patches never influence a visible token (patch-local).
hn candidate windows: every stride-s window inside the episode (t0' in [0, L-1-2s]) within the gap bounds; anchors keep the dataset's existing eligibility (every stride fits).
hn negatives are encoded after every other random draw of the training step, so the rest of the step consumes exactly the random numbers it consumes in chlrm.
hn negatives are drawn with the DataLoader worker's torch generator (seeded by the loader as every other sample choice).
Exports omit the new encoder field 'stem' while it holds its default, so exports of the unchanged method stay readable by earlier code; cs exports carry stem='patch_cnn'.

Fallback chance level: the multi-positive InfoNCE at uniform similarities, ln((16*8-1)/(8-1)) = 2.898 (B = 16 windows x (6 training cameras + 2 synthetic views)); 'at chance' = every logged value (every 50 steps) >= 0.95 x 2.898 = 2.753 over >= 2000 consecutive steps in (10k, 20k] (runs/setup/tools/enc_fallback_check.py).

Diagnostics phase split: gripper open = Meta-World gripper opening obs[3] >= 0.9 (1 = fully open; the directive gives no threshold; fixed before any diagnostic); approach = open and hand-object distance (obs[0:3] vs obs[4:7]) > 3 cm, contact = otherwise.

Diagnostics MLP probe: Linear(D, 256) - GELU - Linear(256, out), inputs and targets standardised on the fit set, AdamW lr 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, batch 256, at most 300 epochs, early stopping with patience 20 epochs on 20 % of the training episodes held back (episode-level split, seed 0), the best held-back epoch restored; fitted on training-camera, training-episode windows, as the ridge probe.

Diagnostics within-episode retrieval: query = a window's state from training camera a; gallery = from camera b != a, the same window and every window of the same episode and stride with 2s+2 <= |t0'-t0| <= 40 (no robot-state rule); top-1 = the same window ranks first (cosine).

fallback_w4_w8.trigger: within the first 20k steps: non-finite loss, or InfoNCE at chance for 2000 consecutive steps after the 10k warm-up (operationalised above)
fallback_w4_w8.action: restart that arm/task once with an encoder-only learning-rate multiplier of 0.6 (train.encoder_lr_mult=0.6; rows enc-<arm>lr06-seed0-<task>-200k, its export and DrM seeds 2000-2002 with evaluators, registered when triggered); report both attempts; the original rows are never stopped

chlrm.hammer, pick-place: completed pilot rows chlrm-*-<task> (mpf-registration-20261023.json, commit e58f1c0, local)
chlrm.bin-picking: registered expansion rows chlrm-seed0-bin-picking-200k, chlrm-export-seed0-bin-picking-200k, chlrm-drm-bin-picking-s2000..2002 and evaluators (chlrm-registration-eight-task-20261024.json); waited for, never duplicated or re-prioritised

behaviour_preservation.cpu_bit_for_bit: tests/test_encoder_pilots.py::test_flags_off_reproduce_the_pre_change_training_bit_for_bit vs tests/data/enc_flags_off_golden.json (written by the unchanged sources, commit ffd4fb8 = main d9fb142): window samples, three chlrm training steps (forward, backward, clipping, AdamW), full-size encoder; flags absent and explicitly off
behaviour_preservation.gpu_fixed_batch: runs/setup/encp-identity-20261025/summary.json: vs the chlrm pilot commit e58f1c0 on 16 real hammer windows with the CUDA renderer: identical resolved config, batch, initial parameters and step-0 states / Gaussians; losses within the same-code GPU run-to-run spread (Chamfer kernel at step 0, atomic rasteriser backward afterwards)

analysis.statistics: IQM; task-stratified bootstrap 95 % CI (B = 2000, seeds resampled within task, arms independent); per-task seed means; returns per task only
analysis.registered: each arm - chlrm, IQM over 9 runs (3 tasks x 3 seeds): hn, cs, h2, w4, w8

factor.w8 - h2: width at depth 8 and head dim 64
factor.w4 - chlrm: SinCro-shaped body vs the current one

analysis.exploratory: each arm - original; each arm - chamfer_lean
analysis.metrics: success last-5, final, AUC (all 100 evaluations) and early AUC (evaluations <= 200k agent steps) for the training, held-out and moving-camera groups
analysis.supplementary: the same pooled contrasts over pick-place + bin-picking only (hammer near ceiling)

diagnostics.scope: inference only, eval mode, no masking (each script asserts not model.training); every new export and the chlrm, chamfer_lean and original exports of the three tasks
diagnostics.renders: pilot-report protocol: 40 validation samples x 22 target cameras, paired by image, episode bootstrap; PSNR / SSIM / LPIPS by camera group (input, novel training, held-out, moving) and region (robot, object, distant background); 3D Chamfer
diagnostics.probes: RL-spaced windows, exact policy state; ridge (as now) and a 2-layer MLP (hidden 256, weight decay, early stopping on held-back training episodes), both fitted on training-camera, training-episode windows; hand and object position and velocity: R^2 and mean Euclidean error (mm); object-minus-hand mean error and spread (mm) by phase (approach = gripper open and hand-object distance > 3 cm; contact = otherwise); transfer to the held-out cameras
diagnostics.retrieval: cross-view top-1 (training, near, trajectory, held-out); within-episode retrieval at gaps in [2s+2, 40]; effective_rank_retrieval; history dependence (cosine to the static-history state); hard-negative cosine with the hn sampler and robot-state rule for every arm
diagnostics.cost: parameters, GFLOPs/frame, median s/it per host, peak GPU memory, pretraining GPU-hours and RL wall time

caveats_to_report: 3 RL seeds and 1 pretraining seed per arm
reference runs from earlier launches / commits / hosts
hn selects negatives with robot state: a binary gate only, never in the loss values; robot state is also the RL proprioception input

review.codex_2026_10_25: P2 retrieval form -> gallery form added; P2 identical masks -> interpretation recorded (same procedure, fresh masks); P3 hand displacement zero -> not a defect (summary transcription; the code subtracts the negative's last frame; test added); test gaps -> two-rank Gloo hn InfoNCE vs concatenated reference, DROID rule, constructed metric values added. No defect found in candidate bounds, cs patch locality, flags-off optimizer/export/RNG paths.
